summary: Adds email search to the user index, update and destroy actions with routes, and a welcome email callback on the User model.

findings.title: Search term interpolated into SQL
findings.problem: The index action puts params[:q] straight into the WHERE clause text. Any authenticated user controls that text.
findings.consequence: An authenticated user can inject SQL to read columns such as api_token or admin. That user can then take over admin accounts.
findings.fix: Pass the search term as a bound parameter and escape LIKE wildcards with sanitize_sql_like.

findings.title: Destroy action exempt from admin check
findings.problem: The change adds destroy to the require_admin exception list. The destroy action then deletes any user found by params[:id].
findings.consequence: Any authenticated user can delete every other user, including admins.
findings.fix: Remove destroy from the except list so the destroy action requires an admin.

findings.title: Welcome email sent on every save
findings.problem: The after_save callback runs on updates as well as creates. The callback also enqueues the mail before the transaction commits.
findings.consequence: Users receive a new welcome email whenever an admin updates them. A rolled back create still enqueues a welcome email.
findings.fix: Use after_create_commit so the mail goes out once after a committed create.

findings.title: New behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: The change adds search, update, destroy and a mail callback. The repository contains no test that exercises any of them.
findings.consequence: Regressions in authorization and search reach production unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add request tests for search, update and destroy, including the non-admin cases, and a model test for the callback.

dropped.reason: The update action stays behind require_admin, so only admins can look up arbitrary users there. This directory app lets admins manage all users.
